# Metric definitions

<!-- Generated by scripts/render_metrics_doc.py from backend/cib/metrics/definitions.py.
     Do not edit by hand: edit the definitions and re-run `make docs`. -->

Every metric the tool computes, in plain language, with exactly which rows it counts and
what it cannot tell you. These definitions are attached to every value the engine returns,
rendered in the dashboard, and printed in the briefing export — so the wording here is the
wording everywhere.

A metric with no definition in `definitions.py` fails the test suite and cannot ship.

## Footprint — how much coverage, and how far it travelled

### Unique stories

`unique_stories` · measured in stories

How many distinct pieces of journalism exist, after collapsing syndicated republications of the same text into one.

**Counts:** One per syndication cluster, plus every article that is in no cluster.

**Caveat:** A cluster is a judgement made by the deduplication pass. Check the cluster list before quoting this figure in a contested setting.

### Unique outlets

`unique_outlets` · measured in outlets

How many separate publications carried the story, counting a syndicated republication as a real appearance because a reader of that outlet did see it.

**Counts:** COUNT(DISTINCT outlet_id) across all articles, before clustering.

### Total articles

`total_articles` · measured in articles

Every imported item, including syndicated duplicates.

**Counts:** Every article row for the campaign within the day-index cutoff.

### Syndication ratio

`syndication_ratio` · measured in outlets per story

How far the average story travelled. 1.0 means every outlet wrote its own piece; 8.0 means one story reached eight outlets.

**Counts:** Unique outlets divided by unique stories.

**Caveat:** A high ratio is wire pickup, not independent interest. It inflates outlet counts without adding newsroom attention.

### Outlet tier mix

`tier_mix` · measured in articles

Where the coverage sits: national press, trade press, wires, NGO channels and so on.

**Counts:** Articles grouped by their outlet's tier, as counts and as a share of all articles.

### Countries

`country_count` · measured in countries

How many countries carried coverage.

**Counts:** COUNT(DISTINCT country) over articles, falling back to the outlet's country when the article row has none.

**Caveat:** Articles with no country on either the article or the outlet are excluded and reported separately as a coverage gap.

### Languages

`language_count` · measured in languages

How many languages the coverage appeared in.

**Counts:** COUNT(DISTINCT language) over articles, falling back to the outlet's language.

### Total reach where sourced

`total_reach` · measured in people

The summed audience of the outlets that carried coverage, counting only outlets whose reach figure comes from a named source.

**Counts:** SUM(outlets.reach_value) over distinct outlets with a non-null reach_value.

**Caveat:** Always read with the reach coverage percentage. If 20% of outlets have a reach figure, this is 20% of an answer, not a total.

### Outlets with a known reach value

`reach_coverage` · measured in %

What share of the outlets carrying this campaign have an audience figure from a named source. This is the honesty check on total reach.

**Counts:** Outlets with a non-null reach_value divided by all outlets carrying the campaign.

## Velocity and persistence — how fast it escalated, how long it lasted

### Peak day

`peak_day` · measured in day index

The day, counted from publication, on which the most articles appeared.

**Counts:** The earliest day_index holding the maximum daily article count. Ties go to the earlier day.

### Peak day volume

`peak_volume` · measured in articles

How many articles appeared on the busiest day.

**Counts:** The maximum daily article count.

### Days to peak

`days_to_peak` · measured in days

How long the story took to reach its busiest day. Zero means it peaked on publication day.

**Counts:** The peak day index itself.

### Half-life

`half_life_days` · measured in days

How many days after the peak it took for daily volume to fall below a tenth of the peak and stay there — a measure of how quickly the story burned out.

**Counts:** Days from the peak day to the first day whose 3-day trailing mean volume is below 10% of the peak volume.

**Caveat:** Null while a campaign is still running or has not yet decayed. A null is not a zero.

### Days to 90% of volume

`days_to_90pct` · measured in days

How long it took to accumulate nine tenths of all the coverage the campaign ever got.

**Counts:** The first day index at which cumulative articles reach 90% of the campaign total.

**Caveat:** Only meaningful once a campaign has finished. Returns null for live campaigns, because the denominator is not final.

### Long tail

`long_tail` · measured in boolean

Whether the campaign was still producing coverage more than 30 days after publication.

**Counts:** True if any article has a day index greater than 30.

## Company exposure — how centrally we appear, and against whom

### Own-company mentions

`own_company_mentions` · measured in mentions

How many times our own company is named, and in what capacity.

**Counts:** Mention rows joining the own_company entity, grouped by role.

**Caveat:** Only counts articles whose body text was imported. Exports without full text cannot be scanned for mentions, and that gap is reported alongside.

### Exposure depth

`depth_score` · measured in weighted points

How central our company is to the coverage, not just how often it appears. Being the subject of a story counts far more than being listed in passing.

**Counts:** Subject x5, named supplier x3, named buyer x3, quoted response x2, passing reference x1, summed across mentions.

**Caveat:** Never quote the total on its own. The components are what make it arguable, and they are always returned with it.

### First mention

`first_mention_day` · measured in day index

The day, counted from publication, on which our company was first named.

**Counts:** The lowest day index among articles containing an own-company mention.

### Named alongside peers

`competitor_comparison` · measured in mentions

Whether we are named more, less, or alongside comparable companies.

**Counts:** Mention counts per entity for own_company and competitor entities, side by side.

## Escalation — what the coverage actually caused

### Escalations

`escalation_count` · measured in events

How many downstream consequences the campaign has produced: legal petitions, regulatory action, customs measures, buyer statements, parliamentary questions, certifier responses.

**Counts:** Escalation rows for the campaign within the day-index cutoff.

**Caveat:** Manually logged. A zero can mean nothing happened or that nobody logged it; the log's last-updated date is shown alongside.

### Days to first escalation

`days_to_first_escalation` · measured in days

How long after publication the first downstream consequence appeared. The sharpest early signal of whether a story is going to become a problem.

**Counts:** Day index of the earliest escalation.

### Severity-weighted escalation total

`severity_weighted_total` · measured in points

Escalations summed by their severity, so one customs measure is not counted the same as one expression of concern.

**Counts:** SUM(severity) across escalations, with the 1-5 anchors listed in the README.

### Escalation chain

`escalation_chain` · measured in stages

How far the campaign travelled along publication to NGO action to regulatory action to buyer action.

**Counts:** The furthest stage reached, with the first event in each stage and the days it took.

## Exposure depth weights

Being the subject of a story is not the same as being listed in passing, so mentions are
weighted by the role the article gives the company:

| Role | Weight |
|---|---|
| subject | ×5 |
| named supplier | ×3 |
| named buyer | ×3 |
| quoted response | ×2 |
| passing reference | ×1 |

The weighted total is never returned without these components. "We scored 34" is exactly
the kind of number this tool exists to replace.

## Escalation severity anchors

A severity-weighted total is only defensible if the scale is written down:

| Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Statement of concern |
| 2 | Formal query or parliamentary question |
| 3 | Buyer, retailer or certifier action |
| 4 | Regulatory investigation opened |
| 5 | Binding regulatory or customs measure, or litigation filed |

## Day index

`day_index` is what makes campaigns comparable: whole days from the campaign's publication
date, measured on calendar dates in the campaign's own timezone.

- **Day 0 is the publication date itself**, not the day after.
- **`day_index` can be negative.** Embargo breaks and pre-publication leaks are real
  coverage; clamping them to zero would hide exactly the thing worth noticing.
- Articles whose date cannot be parsed have a null `day_index`. They are **excluded** from
  every day-truncated figure and reported separately as a data-quality number, never
  folded silently into day 0.

## What is deliberately not a metric

**Sentiment.** Coverage about labour or environmental abuse is negative by construction, so
a tone score does not discriminate between a trade story and a crisis. Tone can be stored
as a secondary label in the `article_tone` table, always with the sentence supporting it,
but no metric function reads that table and no comparison endpoint exposes it. A test
asserts this.
